subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-only embedded dispatch be owned by a generic CLI-backend capability, or may core permanently special-case `claude-cli` credential routing and MCP isolation?
rationale: The patch chooses both an auth-routing ownership boundary and a restricted MCP authorization boundary; tests can verify mechanics but cannot establish the permanent provider/core contract.

options.title: Backend capability flag
options.body: Move eligibility into registered CLI-backend metadata and keep core dispatch generic while retaining grant-level filtering.

options.title: Accept core special-case
options.body: Keep the Claude-only core branch with explicit owner approval and focused upgrade and security proof.

options.title: Use broader routing work
options.body: Pause this PR and fold active-memory into the canonical helper-dispatch design tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57326.

recommendation.title: Backend capability flag
recommendation.body: Move eligibility into registered CLI-backend metadata and keep core dispatch generic while retaining grant-level filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent provider-auth and transcript-boundary work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the auth and security contract choice.
